beats.intro: Lesson twenty-nine. [[sub]]The other difficult task: a valued person tells you, I quit.
beats.dread: This is what Grove dreaded most as a manager. [[val]]A highly valued, respected report decides to leave. [[not]]Not someone chasing more money and better perks elsewhere. [[loyal]]Someone dedicated and loyal, who feels their work is not appreciated. [[lose]]You don't want to lose them, and neither does the company. [[you]]Their decision reflects on you. If their efforts went unrecognized, you have not done your job as their manager.
beats.onrun: The opening shot usually comes when you are on the run. [[minute]]You are hurrying to an important meeting, and they stop you. Do you have a minute? Then, quietly, they say they have decided to leave. [[react]]Your first reaction is absolutely crucial. [[escape]]The human urge is to escape to your meeting, and mumble something about talking later. [[why]]But almost always, they are quitting because they feel unimportant to you. [[confirm]]Put them off, and you confirm it. The outcome is then inevitable. Lesson six said it too: act at once.
beats.q1: Quick check. Pick the right first response.
beats.listen: So, drop what you are doing. [[sit]]Sit them down and ask why they are leaving. [[talk]]Let them talk, and don't argue. They have rehearsed this speech through more than one sleepless night. [[more]]When they have finished their prepared reasons, ask more questions. [[real]]The rehearsed reasons are rarely the real ones. Keep them talking, and the real issues may come out. [[dont]]Don't argue, don't lecture, and don't panic.
beats.skirmish: Remember, this is the opening skirmish, not the war. [[win]]You cannot win the war here, but you can lose it. [[show]]Your job now is to show, by what you do, that they matter to you, [[find]]and to find out what is really troubling them. [[time]]Don't try to change their mind yet. Buy time. Ask for whatever time you need to prepare for the next round. [[keep]]And whatever you commit to, follow through.
beats.boss: Your next move: you have a major problem, so go to your own manager for help. [[busy]]They are probably rushing to an important meeting too, and will want to put it off. [[care]]Not because they don't care, but because it affects you more than them. It is your report who is quitting. [[make]]So make it your manager's problem, and get them to take part in the solution.
beats.citizen: Now corporate citizenship comes in. [[firm]]Your report is a valued employee of the company, not just of your team. [[every]]Pursue every avenue to keep them, even a transfer to another department. [[pm]]If that is the likely answer, become the project manager of that move until it is settled. [[owe]]Why work so hard to keep someone you will lose? Because you owe it to your employer to save a good employee for the company.
beats.golden: Here the golden rule becomes practical. [[today]]Today, you save a valued contributor by practically giving them to a fellow manager. [[tomorrow]]Tomorrow, it is their turn to do the same for you. [[all]]If every manager works this way, in the long run they all win.
beats.back: Now go back with a solution: [[fix]]one that addresses their real reasons for leaving, and also benefits the company. [[obj]]By now they know they matter to you. But they may say: you should have offered this long ago. You only did it because I forced you. [[black]]If I stay, you'll think of me as a blackmailer forever. [[reply]]Make them comfortable with the new arrangement. Something like: you didn't force us into anything we shouldn't have done anyway. [[shook]]You shook us up, and showed us our mistake. We are doing what we should have done all along.
beats.again: Or they may say: I've accepted another job, and I can't back out. [[quit]]Then you have to get them to quit again. [[two]]They really made two commitments. [[new]]One to a new employer they barely know. [[old]]And one to you and their colleagues. [[strong]]A commitment to the people you work with every day is far stronger than one to a casual new acquaintance.
beats.stakes: None of this is easy, for them or for you. [[best]]But give it your best shot, because more is at stake than one person. [[attr]]This person is valuable because of qualities others respect. [[ident]]People like them identify with them. [[watch]]Other strong performers will watch what happens to them, [[morale]]and their own morale and commitment will hinge on the outcome.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]A valued person quitting is a verdict on how you have managed them. [[w2]]Drop everything. Sit them down and let them talk. [[w3]]Don't argue, lecture or panic. Buy time, then deliver. [[w4]]Enlist your manager, and save the person for the company. [[w5]]Answer the blackmail worry, and ask them to quit again. Now the lesson practice.
beats.final1: Lesson practice. Five situations from a manager's week.
beats.finish: Well done. That is the end of lesson twenty-nine.
